who: Historian of modern East Asia, China and Hong Kong at York University from 1991; PhD history, Indiana University, 1977.

evidence.says: York identifies Bernard Luk as its history professor, with an Indiana history PhD in 1977 and a York appointment beginning in 1991.
LC identifies Bernard H. K. Luk as an associate professor at York and records his Indiana University Bloomington PhD thesis, 1977, under Bernard Hung-Kay Luk.

notes: The authority record and university account agree on institution, doctorate and year; the York appointment covers both students.

who: Historian of colonial America and early nineteenth-century United States history at Binghamton, 1960–1988.

evidence.says: Binghamton’s notice identifies Bernard Mason as professor emeritus of history, a colonial and early nineteenth-century US historian, on its faculty from 1960 to 1988.
The University Press of Kentucky’s record for The Road to Independence (1966) identifies author Bernard Mason as associate professor of history at SUNY Binghamton.
LC associates Bernard Mason with The Road to Independence and cites the 1982 Directory of American Scholars identifying him as professor of history at SUNY Binghamton.

notes: The matching authority is the Binghamton historian and author, with a faculty tenure covering 1976 and 1983. The Columbia doctorate was not independently verified.

who: Vernon E. Mattson, historian at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas; PhD, University of Kansas.

evidence.says: LC identifies Vernon E. Mattson as associate professor of history at UNLV in its citation for Frederick Jackson Turner (1985).
The UNLV graduate catalog lists Vernon E. Mattson among history professors emeriti, with an appointment beginning in 1969 and a University of Kansas PhD.
UNLV’s record for Don Franklin Shepherd’s The metahistory of the American West names Vernon Mattson as first committee member.

notes: Full name, institution, doctorate school and a listed student connect the supervisor to Vernon E. Mattson. The repository dates Shepherd’s dissertation 2001, whereas AHA gives 2002.

who: Tracie M. Matysik, European intellectual historian at the University of Texas at Austin; PhD history, Cornell, 2001.

evidence.says: Matysik’s institutional CV records a Cornell history PhD in August 2001 and UT Austin history appointments beginning in 2002.
LC identifies Tracie Matysik with Reforming the Moral Subject and cites her UT Austin history profile: PhD 2001, associate professor, European intellectual history.

notes: The authority’s UT Austin affiliation, field and PhD year match the institutional CV and AHA doctorate.

who: Ronald Timothy McCoy, historian of the American West and American Indian art at Oklahoma State University; PhD, Northern Arizona University, 1983.

evidence.says: LC links Ronald McCoy and Ron McCoy, and records Winter count: the Teton chronicles to 1799 as Ronald T. McCoy’s Northern Arizona University PhD, 1983.
Oklahoma State’s 2010–2011 faculty list names Ron McCoy, PhD, as a professor in History.
The 2016–2017 graduate faculty list identifies Ronald Timothy McCoy as professor emeritus of history with both MA and PhD from Northern Arizona University.

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the Ron/Ronald name link and the exact AHA doctorate school and year; Oklahoma State confirms the full name and history affiliation.

who: Janet Anne Meisel, medieval English historian at the University of Texas at Austin; doctorate, University of California, Berkeley.

evidence.says: LC identifies Janet Meisel, author of Barons of the Welsh Frontier, as a University of California PhD and assistant professor of history at UT Austin.
The Austin American-Statesman obituary describes Meisel as associate professor of medieval English history at UT Austin for 34 years, with a Berkeley doctorate.
UT Austin’s doctoral outcomes page names Janet Meisel as supervisor of The Emergence of a Raiding Society, matching the listed Jansen dissertation.

notes: Institution, field, doctorate school and a listed dissertation support the same identity.

who: Sarah Milov, historian of the modern United States at the University of Virginia; PhD, Princeton University, 2013.

evidence.says: Virginia’s history profile identifies Milov as associate professor, records her Princeton PhD in 2013, and lists The Cigarette: A Political History.
LC identifies the author of The Cigarette as Sarah Milov of Virginia’s Corcoran Department of History, with a Princeton PhD in 2013.
The department’s Spring 2023 dissertation list names Sarah Milov among Crystal Luo’s advisors for Higher Rises, Lower Depths.

notes: Exact institution, PhD school/year, publication and a listed student establish the match.

who: Sharon A. Minichiello, modern Japanese historian at the University of Hawaii at Manoa from 1985; Hawaii PhD, 1975.

evidence.says: The department history lists Sharon A. Minichiello, appointed in 1985, in modern Japan, with Hawaii MA and PhD degrees in 1970 and 1975.
A 2003 university announcement identifies Minichiello as associate professor of history and former director of the Manoa Center for Japanese Studies; she began teaching at UH in 1985.

LC links Sharon and Sharon A. Minichiello to Retreat from Reform and Japan’s Competing Modernities, identifying her as professor of modern Japanese history at Hawaii Manoa and director of its Center for Japanese Studies, 1994–2003.

notes: The authority and institutional sources agree on institution, field and works; the department history also confirms the AHA PhD school and year.
